facts.raw_span: A 63-year-old woman was admitted with insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion and nausea
after an episode of intense acute abdominal pain
She denied hematemesis or melena
untreated dyslipidemia and well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa
She was a smoker of ten cigarettes per day
a palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen
Laboratory tests, including a complete blood count, were normal without anemia
Abdominal ultrasound showed a large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum compatible with an expansive lesion
a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with three Forrest III–type ulcerated areas
biopsy attempts failed to sample the submucosal mass, and ulcer biopsies showed only necrotic mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen demonstrated a well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass arising from the posterior gastric wall, measuring approximately 10×6×11 cm
the lesion had fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture but did not invade the peripheral layers

concepts.why: The patient has a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas, and the mass has fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture on CT, which is consistent with a GIST.
The patient has a large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum compatible with an expansive lesion, and the mass has fat-tissue attenuation on CT, which is consistent with a gastric lipoma.
The patient has a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas, which is consistent with a gastric carcinoma.
The patient has a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas, which is consistent with a gastric lymphoma.
The patient has insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion and nausea, which is consistent with peptic ulcer disease.
The patient has untreated dyslipidemia, which is consistent with dyslipidemia.
The patient has well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa, which is consistent with hypertension.
The patient is a smoker of ten cigarettes per day, which increases the risk of smoking-related illnesses.

rationales.F05: Smoking is a risk factor for various diseases, including gastric carcinoma and lymphoma.
rationales.F09: The presence of a submucosal bulging mass with ulcerated areas is highly suggestive of a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST).
rationales.F11: The CT scan findings of a well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass with fat-tissue attenuation are highly suggestive of a gastric lipoma.
rationales.F12: The presence of fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement and trabecular architecture is highly suggestive of a gastric lipoma, while the absence of invasion into peripheral layers rules out gastric carcinoma and lymphoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas and the CT findings of a well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass with fat-tissue attenuation and central contrast enhancement are more consistent with a GIST, despite the high specificity of fat-tissue attenuation for lipoma.
